work:linkedin-growth-loop.category: High-autonomy agents, Agent orchestration, Browser control, Trace-based evals

systemMap.label: Daily list
systemMap.description: CRM and LinkedIn Navigator sources produced a bounded list of people to inspect, score, and act on.

systemMap.label: Networking Connector
systemMap.description: Handles target discovery, scoring, queueing, connection-note generation, send-or-skip decisions, and follow-up state.

systemMap.label: Feed Engager
systemMap.description: Reads relevant feed and target-audience posts, scores fit, respects cooldowns, checks duplicates, and records interaction outcomes.

systemMap.label: OpenClaw orchestrator
systemMap.description: Runs the agent lanes, coordinates reporting, and owns the improvement path around observed outcomes.

systemMap.label: Hermes research advisor
systemMap.description: Collects outside research, platform drift, memory context, and risk signals before future changes are proposed.

systemMap.label: Telegram control room
systemMap.description: Shows human-readable summaries first, then keeps run details, metrics, proof trail, and controls available underneath.

systemMap.label: Learning history
systemMap.description: Preserves accepted, pending, failed, skipped, response, run-note, good-example, and proposed-change signals for future review.

systemMap.label: Cost-aware browser control
systemMap.description: Uses programmatic SOPs, page calibration, recorder flows, and minimal-intelligence recovery before paying for heavier model judgment.

sections.title: Agents Are Overhyped Until They Own The Work
The In-House Need Made It Serious
LinkedIn Became The First Real Success
Browser Control Kept The Cost Honest
One Failure That Forced Better Rules
What Moved Out Of My Head

oak: Designed and implemented the bounded relationship workflow, starting from CRM and LinkedIn Navigator target lists and expanding into connector and feed-engagement agent lanes.
Built the Telegram control room so run summaries, metrics, run details, and operator controls stayed readable instead of becoming another pile of logs.
Paired OpenClaw as the worker/orchestrator with Hermes as the research and improvement advisor so execution, research, evaluation, and improvement could work together.
Designed cost-aware browser-control paths with programmatic SOPs, page calibration, recorder flows, and selective model calls for judgment-heavy steps.
collaborators: No project collaborators are confirmed for this internal build.

External platforms and tools include LinkedIn, Telegram Bot API, Convex, Playwright/Patchright, OpenClaw, Hermes, model providers, and related agent frameworks. Avoid describing them as sponsors, partners, endorsers, or proof of platform approval.

systemMap.label: Short-term context
systemMap.description: Keep the current task, constraints, active files, and working decisions close enough for the next agent step.

systemMap.label: Durable memory
systemMap.description: Store cross-session decisions, taste rules, failure history, and source references where future sessions can retrieve them.

systemMap.label: Retrieval
systemMap.description: Route questions through RAG, contextual codebase search, Graphify, wiki pages, or direct source reads depending on what needs to be trusted.

systemMap.label: Instruction surfaces
systemMap.description: Use AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills, and plugin instructions to make repeated behavior explicit instead of relying on chat memory.

systemMap.label: MCP collections
systemMap.description: Group specialized external and local tools so agents can reach the right source, action, or dataset without rebuilding the route each time.

oak: Experimented across short-term and long-term memory techniques for agentic development workflows.
Compared RAG, contextual codebase search, context engines, memory graphs, Obsidian-style graph workflows, instruction-file management, and MCP collections as practical memory surfaces.
Designed the public case-study boundary so the page can explain the system shape before the full article, diagrams, and screenshots are ready.
collaborators: Public collaborator and tool attribution is not yet finalized.
Named techniques describe workflow categories, not tool sponsorship, endorsement, or official integration claims.
